subject: Architecture review: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & autoscaling
messages:
From: Kate Lin <kate.lin@novusanalytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: dedicated GPU capacity architecture deep-dive

Sergio / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Novus wants to follow up with a technical deep-dive focused on Dedicated capacity. Primary topics we want covered: pool sizing guidance for our workload, autoscaling behavior under bursty traffic, and isolation/tenant boundaries for our data-sensitive workloads.

A few context points so the session can be targeted:
- Production traffic estimate: peak ~250 concurrent requests (inference calls) with occasional sustained bursts up to 400 for ~10–20m.
- Typical payload: LLM (quantized Llama2-13B variant), average sequence length ~1k tokens, KV cache per-request expected.
- Security: strict separation between Novus and co-tenants required; we’ll need to understand network-level isolation and host tenancy options.
- Timeline: procurement decision target by end of Q2.

Would you be able to schedule a 60–75 minute architecture review with your solutions engineering and product folks next week? Timezone: Pacific. Our core attendees will be myself, our infra lead (ops@novusanalytics.com), and one of our ML infra engineers.

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Lin
Director, Cloud Platform
Novus Analytics

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate.lin@novusanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated GPU capacity architecture deep-dive

Hi Kate — great to hear the demo landed well. Happy to run the architecture review. Proposed agenda (60–75m):
1) Quick run-through of Novus workload profile & goals (10m)
2) Dedicated pool sizing scenarios (Rafael) — baseline, peak, and burst strategies (25m)
3) Autoscaling semantics and latency tradeoffs (15m)
4) Isolation & network tenancy options, KMS/HSM touchpoints (10m)
5) Open Q&A & next steps (10–15m)

Available slots (Pacific):
- Tue 17 Mar, 10:00–11:15
- Tue 17 Mar, 15:00–16:15
- Wed 18 Mar, 09:00–10:15

I’ll attach a preliminary capacity spreadsheet and a short network diagram to make the pre-read productive. Rafael will prepare three pool-sizing scenarios (steady, burst-capacity with warm standby, and aggressive autoscale). If you want Vivek on the call to discuss SLA tiers and routing/fallback policies, we can bring him.

Pre-reads attached: prelim_capacity_estimate.xlsx, network_diag_v1.png

If those times don’t work, tell us what does and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Kate Lin <kate.lin@novusanalytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novusanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated GPU capacity architecture deep-dive

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 09:03 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Kate — great to hear the demo landed well. Happy to run the architecture review. Proposed agenda (60–75m):
> ...

Thanks — those agenda items look spot on. We do need to shift the week-of date due to a supplier review that just popped up. Can we move to Thu 19 Mar, 09:30–10:45 PT or Fri 20 Mar, 11:00–12:15 PT? Thu morning is my preference.

Also a couple clarifications so Rafael can size correctly:
- When you say “warm standby” in burst strategy, are you assuming pre-warmed workers (persistent GPUs) or rapid cold-start via pre-loaded model snapshots?
- We definitely want to dive deeper on isolation: we need to understand lane-level RBAC, whether node isolation (dedicated host) is available, and the degree of audit logging for KV cache access.

Procurement note: legal will want a short note on where data is persisted during inference and whether KV cache may be offloaded to customer-controlled storage. If you can include a short pointer to that during the call, that would be useful.

Kate

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate.lin@novusanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated GPU capacity architecture deep-dive

Kate — thanks for the heads up, Thu 19 Mar 09:30–10:45 PT works for us. I’ve gone ahead and sent a calendar invite (calendar_invite.ics) and added a brief pre-read folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gx-example-pre-read

Quick answers to your clarifying questions so Rafael can prep:
- "Warm standby" scenario = hybrid: a small pool of pre-warmed instances to guarantee sub-100ms cold-starts for high-priority requests + fast scale-up path via snapshot restore for larger bursts. Rafael will present memory/kv-cache sizing that shows tradeoffs.
- Isolation: we support dedicated host allocation for strict tenancy, VPC-level isolation, and per-tenant encryption keys. We’ll include an audit-log reference during the session and show where KV cache access is logged and how long entries persist by default.
- Data persistence: Redwood’s runtime keeps KV cache in-memory by default; offload to customer-controlled blob (S3/compatible) is an option for long-lived caches — Rafael will show patterns and expected latency impact.

Action items before the call:
- Rafael: prepare three capacity scenarios + one slide on KV persistence tradeoffs.
- Vivek: prepare a short note on SLA tiers and routing fallbacks.
- Monica: coordinate Ops/CS presence and confirm the invite list.

See you Thu 19 Mar 09:30 PT.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
